Title: A step ahead from primary care: Advance Nurse Practitioner programme of AKUH
NewsSummary: The Department of Surgery, Cardiothoracic section, in collaboration with AKU School of Nursing and Midwifery, has initiated the first-ever Advance Nurse Practitioner programme in Pakistan.
NewsContent:
"The Department of Surgery, Cardiothoracic section, in collaboration with AKU School of Nursing and Midwifery, has initiated the first-ever Advance Nurse Practitioner programme in Pakistan. This is a one year, on-the-job training programme which involves advance level teaching and supervision of five mid-level nurses working at the cardiac intensive care unit at Aga Khan University Hospital.

As advance NPs, these nurses will assume independent positions in a designated setting and will complement residents and interns who attend patients intermittently. They will provide dedicated end-to-end pre and post-operative care, from initially obtaining health history to planning of care and modifying it as per the attending surgeon’s preference and advice. Handling a case holistically and seamlessly, they will not only perform various patient care and administrative activities, but will also assist surgeons and physicians in research studies by efficiently maintaining databases. 

Dr Sulaiman Hasan, Head and Consultant, cardiothoracic surgery, Department of Surgery is one of the six experienced cardiothoracic surgeons who will be providing this training. Talking about the role of nurse practitioners, Dr Hasan said, “They are a different component of medical care just like doctors, nurses and management staff. They will be doing things that are currently done by doctors. Further down the road they will have a very good handle on the data and involving them in any research could be done smoothly.”

The competency based modular programme developed by SONAM leads to a certificate issued by SONAM and signed off by the surgeons. 

Advance Nurse Practitioner programme is the first initiative of its kind in Pakistan and is a part of constant, however, subtle change in nursing practice in Pakistan. Increased and transformed healthcare needs require more formal education and additional training for healthcare professionals, especially nurses. Once complete, this programme will yield results with improved patient care. "
